_comment: Per-gene predictability diagnostic (DESIGN v3 section 4 'Per-gene predictability', RESEARCH_TREE D22). Every method and threshold below is declared and committed BEFORE the per-gene tier distribution, the characterisation statistics or the biomarker comparison are computed. Diagnostic only: headline P1, the selection rule, delta, gene classes, labels and metrics are unchanged. Read by src/essml/predictability.py, scripts/predictability_tiers.py, scripts/predictability_characterise.py, scripts/evaluate_test.py and scripts/predict.py.

source.role: G4 headline model (m1_E_resB0 unless G3 selects another; recompute with --run if M5 becomes the headline)
source.predictions: cache/runs/<run_id>/pred.parquet (dev-CV out-of-fold predictions); if absent, re-run the config with scripts/run.py

per_fold_r.definition: r_g,k = Pearson r across the held-out lines of outer fold k, computed by the frozen essml.evaluate (single call, fold_of_line = configs/splits.csv cv_fold, genes = all predicted genes, gene classes = configs/gene_classes.csv); NaN where the gene has fewer than min_obs observed held-out lines (evaluate's min_obs rule); constant predictions give r = 0 (frozen convention).
per_fold_r.sd_r: fold SD, ddof = 1 (as evaluate's fold SDs)
per_fold_r.check: the recomputed per-fold r must equal the run's cached cache/runs/<run_id>/per_gene_fold.parquet r on the eval genes (|diff| <= 1e-9) when that file exists

tiers.evaluable: evaluable (finite r) in every fold of per_fold_r.folds; otherwise tier 'not_evaluable' (no confidence score)
tiers.high: mean_r >= T_high (T_high = 0.30 unless escalated) and min_r >= 0.20
tiers.comparison: inclusive (>=) where DESIGN says >=, strict where it says >; values are compared in float64 without rounding

confidence: clip(mean_r - sd_r, -1, 1) for evaluable genes; NaN for not_evaluable genes

null_calibration.definition: the same per-fold r, tiers and thresholds on the null control's out-of-fold predictions; expected false high = number of null genes that are 'high'
null_calibration.rule: if n_high(null, 0.30) > 0.05 * n_high(observed, 0.30), raise T_high (only) to the smallest value in the ladder at which n_high(null, T) <= 0.05 * n_high(observed, T); medium is unchanged. This is the only allowed adjustment and it is recorded in results/predictability/distribution.json and in the threshold column of configs/predictable_genes.csv.
null_calibration.if_no_ladder_value_passes: use 0.50 (the top of the ladder), record status 'ladder_exhausted' and flag for the PI
null_calibration.estimated_fdr: n_high(null) / n_high(observed) at the threshold used (also reported at every ladder value)

outputs.table: configs/predictable_genes.csv: entrez, symbol, r_fold0..r_fold4, mean_r, min_r, sd_r, n_folds_evaluable, confidence, tier, source_run_id, threshold_high_mean_r (one row per predicted gene)
outputs.distribution: results/predictability/distribution.json: quantiles and histogram of mean_r (all evaluable and variable genes), tier counts, null counts, estimated FDR, per-gene P2b (normalised AP, AUROC) by tier

p2b_by_tier: per gene and fold, the frozen evaluate's nap / auroc (>= 3 positives and >= 3 negatives, label effect < -0.5); the per-gene value is the mean over folds where defined. Reported for selective genes (configs/gene_classes.csv) with headline-style restriction (fold prevalence <= 0.5 in every fold used) and without it.

dry_run.purpose: G4 dry run (scripts/evaluate_test.py --dry-run-dev): dev fold 0 stands in for the test set, so the tiers used there are computed from folds 1-4 only (fold 0's own CV results are not used). Disclosure: the fold 1-4 models were trained on lines that include fold 0.

characterisation.population: dev lines only (configs/splits.csv role == dev); CRISPR values only via essml.guard.load_targets(dev IDs)
characterisation.comparisons: tiers high / medium / low (not_evaluable excluded). Continuous gene properties: per-tier median and IQR; high vs low and medium vs low: difference in medians with a 95% gene-bootstrap CI (2000 resamples, seed 20261026), rank-biserial correlation and Mann-Whitney U p; Kruskal-Wallis across the three tiers; Spearman correlation of the property with mean_r across evaluable genes (gene-bootstrap CI). Binary properties: per-tier fraction, odds ratio high vs low with Woolf 95% CI and Fisher exact p. Genes are not independent (co-regulated, shared lines), so p-values and gene-bootstrap CIs are descriptive.
characterisation.gene_effect: from all dev lines (observed only): SD (ddof 1), mean and fraction of lines < -0.5 (configs/gene_classes.csv sd / frac_below; mean recomputed from guarded dev targets)
characterisation.gene_class: configs/gene_classes.csv classes variable, selective, rare_selective, common_essential, nonessential: tier x class counts and fractions

primary.name: lineage_mean_crosslib_01
primary.method: Library groups = configs/library_groups.csv lib_group (dev NaN-pattern groups). For each gene, per-lineage mean gene effect over the observed dev lines of library group 0 and, separately, of library group 1, for lineages (configs/splits.csv OncotreeLineage) with >= 5 dev lines in BOTH groups; a lineage mean needs >= 3 observed lines of the gene in that group. Reliability = Pearson r across eligible lineages of the two vectors of lineage means; NaN if fewer than 5 lineages have both means.

anchor_agreement.name: external_anchor_agreement
anchor_agreement.method: External anchor screens of DepMap DEV lines only (results/harmonisation/anchor_agreement.csv role == anchor; 23 screens of 18 dev lines), profile = cache/harmonised/anchor_LOAO_location__<anchor id>.parquet column loao_corrected (affine + gene-wise location correction fitted WITHOUT that anchor), read only through essml.guard.load_harmonised(name, anchor_model_id=<dev ModelID>) (guard-approved anchor reader; each read is logged). Per gene: Pearson r across anchor screens between the external effect and the DepMap gene effect of the same dev line; genes need >= 15 anchor screens with both values. Descriptive (most anchors are AML lines).

characterisation.biomarker_pairs: configs/biomarker_pairs.csv (committed before the comparison): report each pair's dependency-gene tier, mean_r and whether the biomarker is a headline-model input (the headline uses expression only).
characterisation.own_expression: per gene, Pearson r across dev lines between the gene's own expression (cache/features/E.parquet, log2(TPM+1), column = Entrez) and its gene effect, observed lines only; genes absent from E -> NaN. Reported signed and as |r|.
characterisation.paralog: cache/priors/paralog_top.parquet (Ensembl 116 Compara): has_paralog = family_size_id20 > 0 (a paralog with >= 20% identity); max_identity (0 if none); high-identity paralog = max_identity >= 50.

collections.reactome: data/raw_external/reactome_gmt/ReactomePathways.gmt.zip, symbols mapped to Entrez via configs/gene_classes.csv DepMap symbols, then HGNC approved symbols, then unique previous/alias symbols

tests.high_vs_evaluable: foreground = high tier; background = all evaluable genes (tiers high/medium/low)
tests.low_among_variable: foreground = low tier among variable evaluable genes; background = variable evaluable genes

enrichment.set_size: gene sets restricted to the background; tested if 10 <= size <= 500
enrichment.statistic: one-sided hypergeometric over-representation P(X >= k); BH within each collection x test; report odds ratio and fold enrichment
enrichment.report: sets with BH q < 0.05, top 15 by q per collection x test

test_reporting.per_tier: P1 (all genes of the tier, and tier x variable) and P2b normalised AP / AUROC (selective genes of the tier, prevalence <= 0.5) from the frozen evaluate's per-gene output, with patient-bootstrap CIs as the headline (essml.heldout).
test_reporting.transfer_check: Spearman correlation across evaluable genes between dev mean_r and test r_g, with a patient-bootstrap percentile CI (same draws as the headline bootstrap).
test_reporting.precondition: scripts/evaluate_test.py refuses to run unless configs/predictable_genes.csv is committed (tracked and unmodified) and records its sha256 in every output.
